title: Event Cleanup
summary: Connections you create are yours to remove: store the RBXScriptConnection, Disconnect when the reaction should stop — especially for per-spawn, per-round, and short-lived-object handlers. Leaked connections accumulate forever.

explanation.whatItIs: Hygiene for event wiring: every Connect has a matching 'when do I Disconnect?' answer.
explanation.whyItExists: Connections keep their handler functions (and everything they reference) alive. Forgotten connections run forever — duplicated work, growing memory.
whenToUse: Per-spawn handlers: connect in CharacterAdded, disconnect on Died/CharacterRemoving
Round systems: connect at round start, disconnect at round end
Short-lived objects (projectiles, traps): disconnect in the same code path that destroys them
One-shots: use :Once() and skip manual cleanup
whenNotToUse: Lifetime-of-game connections from a script that itself lives forever — nothing to clean
explanation.mentalModel:
```text
Every Connect answers two questions:
  1. who owns this wire?
  2. when does it end?

connect on spawn ──▶ disconnect on death
connect on round ──▶ disconnect on round end
Once()           ──▶ auto
```
tips: Keep connections in a table per system; a cleanup loop Disconnects all
conn.Connected tells you if it's still live
Destroying an object kills connections TO its events — but not connections you added to OTHER events watching it
commonMistakes: CharacterAdded connecting Humanoid.Died every respawn without disconnecting the old ones — N deaths fire the handler N times
Loop-spawning parts with Touched handlers, never cleaned
Holding connection tables that outlive their purpose (memory)

examples.title: Per-life wiring, done right
examples.code:
Players.PlayerAdded:Connect(function(player)
    player.CharacterAdded:Connect(function(character)
        local humanoid = character:WaitForChild("Humanoid")

        local diedConn
        diedConn = humanoid.Died:Once(function()
            -- once = auto-disconnect
            handleDeath(player)
        end)

        -- Example: manual lifecycle connection
        local stepConn = game:GetService("RunService").Heartbeat:Connect(function(dt)
            -- regen tick
        end)

        humanoid.Died:Once(function()
            stepConn:Disconnect()   -- stop the tick at death
        end)
    end)
end)
